title: "Shiny module trees"
guide-section: "Shiny"

A Shiny for Python app spreads its work across modules, reactive functions, and helpers in several files. On this page I'll draw that structure with two functions. `call_tree_dir()` reads `.py` files on disk, and `call_tree_app()` inspects a `shiny.App` object.

## A small app

The code below writes a small app to a temporary folder. It has one module pair, a helper module imported under an alias, and a class with one shared instance:

```{python}
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

app_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "counter"
app_dir.mkdir()
(app_dir / "__init__.py").write_text("")
(app_dir / "labels.py").write_text('''
def clean(text):
    return text.strip()


class Labeler:
    def label(self, text):
        return clean(text).title()
''')
(app_dir / "modules.py").write_text('''
from shiny import module, render, ui

from . import labels as lb

_labeler = lb.Labeler()


def log_msg(msg):
    return msg


@module.ui
def counter_ui(label="Count"):
    log_msg("counter_ui")
    return ui.input_action_button("go", _labeler.label(label))


@module.server
def counter_server(input, output, session):
    log_msg("counter_server")

    @render.text
    def count():
        return str(input.go())
''')
_ = (app_dir / "app.py").write_text('''
import shiny
from shiny import App, ui

from .modules import counter_server, counter_ui, log_msg


def app_ui():
    return ui.page_fluid(counter_ui("a"))


def app_server(input, output, session):
    log_msg("server")
    counter_server("a")


app = App(app_ui(), app_server)


def run_app():
    shiny.run_app("counter.app:app")
''')
```

## Reading the files

`call_tree_dir()` parses every `.py` file under `path` without importing it. Each top level function is linked to the functions its body calls or names:

```{python}
from callgrove import call_tree_dir

call_tree_dir(app_dir, root="app_server")
```

`counter_server.count` is the `@render.text` function defined inside `counter_server`. Every decorated function nested in another one gets its own node, labeled `outer.inner`. That covers Shiny's `@reactive.effect`, `@reactive.calc`, and `@render.*` functions. A repeated name such as `_` gets `#2`, `#3`, and so on. Undecorated helpers defined inside a function stay folded into it.

`log_msg` shows up under every node. `exclude` drops it and moves its children up:

```{python}
call_tree_dir(app_dir, root="app_server", exclude="log_msg")
```

When two files define a function with the same name, `call_tree_dir()` warns and keeps the one parsed last.

## Following imports and aliases

`counter_ui()` calls `_labeler.label()`, and nothing in that name says where `label` is defined. `call_tree_dir()` works it out from the file's imports and assignments, the same way Python would:

```{mermaid}
%%| eval: true
%%| fig-align: 'center'
%%| fig-caption: 'How _labeler.label() is resolved'
%%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "fontSize":"18px", "darkMode":false}}}%%

flowchart TD
    ref(["<code>_labeler.label()</code><br>in <code>modules.py</code>"])
    assign("<code>_labeler = lb.Labeler()</code><br>a module level instance")
    imp("<code>from . import</code><br><code>labels as lb</code>")
    cls[["<code>class Labeler</code><br>in <code>labels.py</code>"]]
    node[/"node <code>Labeler.label</code>"/]

    ref -->|"i. look up <code>_labeler</code>"| assign
    assign -->|"ii. look up <code>lb</code>"| imp
    imp -->|"iii. find <code>Labeler</code>"| cls
    cls -->|"iv. find the <code>label</code> method"| node

    style ref fill:#FFFFFF,stroke:#3E2A1E
    style assign fill:#2A6F77,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
    style imp fill:#2A6F77,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5
    style cls fill:#fff,stroke:#3E2A1E
    style node fill:#E8A33D,color:#1B2A41
```

The tree below shows the result. Nodes use the name of the definition (`Labeler.label`), not the alias at the call site:

```{python}
call_tree_dir(app_dir, root="counter_ui")
```

The same lookup handles the other common forms:

* Aliased module: `mdl.fit()` after `import pkg.model as mdl`.
* Relative module: `plots.draw()` after `from . import plots`.
* Renamed function: `g()` after `from .m import f as g`.

Class methods can also be roots. `call_tree_dir(app_dir, root="Labeler.label")` starts the tree at that method.

## Launch strings

A launch function usually names the app as a string, which `shiny.run_app()` imports later. `call_tree_dir()` follows a `"module:attr"` string when the module is one of the scanned files. The string becomes a node. Its children are the functions that the `app = ...` assignment calls or names:

```{python}
call_tree_dir(app_dir, root="run_app", exclude="log_msg")
```

Sometimes the string names a function instead, such as an app factory in `"counter.app:create_app"`. The tree then links straight to that function. A string that points outside the scanned folder is ignored.

## Modules only

`modules_only=True` keeps the root and the functions decorated with `@module.ui` or `@module.server`. Every other function is spliced out, nested reactive functions included, and its children move up:

```{python}
call_tree_dir(app_dir, root="app_ui", modules_only=True)
```

## Inspecting an App object

`call_tree_app()` takes the server out of a `shiny.App` and follows the names it references. Only functions defined in the app's own package join the tree, so `shiny.ui` calls are left out. The app is never run:

```{python}
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(app_dir.parent))
from counter.app import app
from callgrove import call_tree_app

call_tree_app(app, exclude="log_msg")
```

`App()` renders a static UI when it is created, so the function behind it is gone. That's why the tree above has no UI branch, and why `call_tree_app()` warned about it. Pass the function's name with `ui_fun` to add the UI branch:

```{python}
call_tree_app(app, ui_fun="app_ui", exclude="log_msg")
```

Module functions are found even though Shiny wraps them, because `call_tree_app()` peels the decorator off before reading the source. Here the nodes keep the name written at the call site (`_labeler.label`), because `call_tree_app()` looks each name up in the running module.

## Recap

`call_tree_dir()` works on source you haven't installed, and it resolves imports, aliases, and methods without running anything. `call_tree_app()` works on an app you can import. Both return a `CallTree` and take `modules_only`, `exclude`, and `max_depth`.
